headline: RBI issues draft directions on preventive safeguards for electronic banking transactions
summary_points: RBI has issued draft Amendment Directions on preventive safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs) for public comments.
The drafts aim to give customers greater control over the manner and extent to which digital payment channels may be used.
The scope of 'negligence by a bank' defined in the 24 June 2026 Amendment Directions is proposed to be expanded.
Comments are invited from regulated entities and the public on or before 14 December 2026.
who_is_affected: Commercial, small finance, payments, local area, regional rural and co-operative banks, and their customers who use digital payment channels.
action_required: Banks and other stakeholders should review the drafts and submit feedback via the 'Connect 2 Regulate' section of the RBI website or by email on or before 14 December 2026.

social.linkedin:
RBI has issued draft Amendment Directions on 'Preventive Safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs)' for public comments.

The June 24, 2026 Amendment Directions on customer protection in fraudulent EBTs strengthened the framework on limiting customer liability. The new drafts add a preventive angle by proposing to give customers greater control over how, and to what extent, digital payment channels can be used.

The drafts also propose to expand the definition of 'negligence by a bank' to bring uniformity in bank practices and protect customers against specific acts of omission or commission by banks.

Seven sets of draft Amendment Directions amending the Responsible Business Conduct Directions have been issued, covering commercial banks, small finance banks, payments banks, local area banks, regional rural banks, and urban and rural co-operative banks.

Comments can be submitted by December 14, 2026 through the 'Connect 2 Regulate' section of the RBI website or by email.

Please verify the details with the official RBI source before acting.
